document.title: Technical Documentation: Zero to Agent Jerusalem

sections.title: Program Overview
sections.content: The AI Collective Jerusalem is conducting an intensive technical workshop on April 28, 2026. This curriculum facilitates a transition from conceptualization to deployment via three progressive stages: Interaction, Control, and Architecture.

sections.title: Fundamental Tier: Interaction
sections.objective: Establish foundational competence and technical orientation in agentic systems.

concepts.name: Agent Definition
concepts.description: Autonomous systems utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) for reasoning, tool orchestration, and task completion.

concepts.name: Prompt Engineering
concepts.description: Distinction between user inputs, system instructions, and external tool definitions.

concepts.name: Interface Protocols
concepts.description: Utilization of APIs to facilitate communication between applications and the Gemini model.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.description: An open-source AI assistant that brings Google's Gemini model to the terminal for code analysis, debugging, and tool orchestration.

tools.name: Google Antigravity
tools.description: A task-oriented agentic development platform that allows developers to orchestrate autonomous agents for planning and executing complex tasks.

prerequisites.name: Node.js
prerequisites.description: Install the latest LTS version. Verify by running node -v in your terminal.
prerequisites.installation_note: Click on the Windows Installer (.msi) link on the official Node.js website.

prerequisites.name: Terminal
prerequisites.description: Use PowerShell or CMD (Windows), Terminal (macOS), or Bash/Zsh (Linux). Terminals are included by default on all three operating systems. Windows users are recommended to install Git Bash.

prerequisites.name: Gemini API Key
prerequisites.description: API keys will be distributed at the beginning of the event. If you did not receive yours, please contact the staff team.

steps.notes: Requires a terminal and Node.js installed. If the command fails, refer to section 2.2.1. Linux users should prefix the command with sudo.
Provide your API key when prompted.

steps.description: Adding the Vercel MCP (Model Context Protocol) to Gemini allows the CLI to be more accurate. Gemini CLI shares the same configuration as Gemini Code Assist.
sub_steps: Ensure you have the Gemini CLI installed.
Add the following configuration to your ~/.gemini/settings.json file: { "mcpServers": { "vercel": { "command": "npx", "args": ["mcp-remote", "https://mcp.vercel.com"] } } }
Run the Gemini CLI and use the /mcp list command to see available MCP servers.
When prompted, authenticate with Vercel to grant access.

subsections.title: Project Setup: Gemini.md File
subsections.description: Download the Gemini.md file from the provided GitHub profile (link pending) and place it directly into your project's root folder.

steps.description: Navigate to the Antigravity web portal.
Create a new workspace and integrate your Gemini API key in the settings to enable agent orchestration.

concepts.name: Prompt-First Development
concepts.description: Writing instructions in natural language before writing a single line of code.

concepts.name: The Iteration Loop
concepts.note: Non-engineers can use AI chatbots to refine simple requests into detailed technical prompts.

example.description: To create a website showcasing cats, a prompt was provided to ChatGPT asking it to generate a Gemini CLI prompt using Node.js, Vercel, and Next.js.

generated_prompt.title: Build a modern, responsive cat showcase website
core_requirements: Clean, playful, cat-themed design (soft colors, rounded UI, smooth animations)

features.name: Homepage
details: Hero section with a title like 'Meet My Cats'
Featured cat cards with image, name, and short description

features.name: Gallery Page
details: Masonry or grid layout of all cat photos

features.name: About Page
details: Short story about me and my cats

features.name: Admin-Friendly Data Structure
details: Store cat data in a local JSON file or mock CMS structure

technical_requirements: Use Next.js Image component for optimization
Use dynamic routing for cat pages
Include SEO metadata (title, description per page)
Add loading states and error handling

concepts.name: Structuring Instructions
concepts.description: Using clear delimiters and specific constraints.

concepts.name: Simple Chaining
concepts.description: Breaking complex tasks into a sequence of smaller, manageable prompts.
concepts.example: Instead of 'put all items in the middle,' prompt the AI to center all elements within a specific div (providing the div ID).

subsections.title: Code Samples from The Official Documentation

packages.name: ai
packages.description: The AI SDK is a provider-agnostic TypeScript toolkit designed to help you build AI-powered applications and agents using popular UI frameworks like Next.js, React, Svelte, Vue, Angular, and runtimes like Node.js.

packages.name: dotenv
packages.description: A zero-dependency module that loads environment variables from a .env file into process.env. Based on The Twelve-Factor App methodology.

api_key_setup.description: Create an API key in your Vercel dashboard and save it to your environment file.
api_key_setup.note: The API key should be created on the Vercel Platform.

code_sample.description: Test your setup (this can be skipped)
code_sample.further_resources: For more advanced examples, see the official docs: Templates section.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.description: A tool that enables Gemini to operate within the terminal and interact with code directly.
tools.usage: After installation, open your terminal and type gemini. The interface features a terminal screen with a central text input. Paste your prompt into this input to begin coding.

tools.name: Antigravity
tools.description: Google Antigravity is an AI-assisted code editor.
tools.usage: Use the chat interface on the right to start coding with the AI.

subsections.title: Level I Capstone
subsections.example: Training platform for writing formal texts.
requirements: Must provide a formatted response based on specific system instructions.

sections.title: Intermediate Tier: Control
sections.objective: Scale the project by implementing multiple functionalities and pages. For advanced workflows, begin building and connecting multiple services.

concepts.name: Function/Tool Calling
concepts.description: Teaching the agent to interact with real-world data (e.g., checking weather, searching a database). Vercel enables the generation of a MongoDB Atlas database with only a few clicks.

concepts.name: Structured Outputs
concepts.description: Forcing the model to return valid JSON schemas for programmatic use.

concepts.name: Short-term Memory
concepts.description: Implementing chat history objects to maintain conversational threads.

concepts.name: Basic Persistence
concepts.description: Saving user preferences or session data to simple storage.

concepts.name: Failure Analysis
concepts.description: Determining if a failure occurred due to the base prompt, system constraints, or a tool error.

concepts.name: Refinement
concepts.description: Adjusting temperature and top-up settings to control creativity vs. reliability.

concepts.name: Separation of Concerns
concepts.description: Keeping logic for tool execution separate from the prompt logic.

subsections.title: Level II Capstone
requirements: The system must utilize at least one external tool or API call.

sections.title: Advanced Tier: Architecture
sections.objective: Design production-grade AI architectures under enterprise constraints.

concepts.name: Collaboration Patterns
concepts.description: Implementing 'Swarm' or 'Orchestrator' patterns.

concepts.name: Role-Based Specialized Agents
concepts.description: Defining specific personas for Planning, Execution, and Review/Validation.

concepts.name: Scalability
concepts.description: Why raw prompts fail with large datasets.

concepts.name: Vector Databases
concepts.description: Using embeddings to retrieve relevant context before the model call.

concepts.name: Trade-off Analysis
concepts.description: Balancing latency, cost, and retrieval accuracy.

concepts.name: Decision Logging
concepts.description: Tracing the agent's reasoning steps to understand 'why' it took an action.

concepts.name: Cost Engineering
concepts.description: Token optimization and implementing caching strategies to reduce API spend.

concepts.name: Safety Guardrails
concepts.description: Input validation and output constraints to prevent hallucinations in critical flows.

concepts.name: Full-Stack Integration
concepts.description: Designing the backend service, API layer, and frontend (v0/Next.js).

concepts.name: Deployment
concepts.description: Moving the agent system to Vercel for global availability.

options.description: A Research Agent with a full RAG pipeline.
A Multi-step Workflow Automation Agent (e.g., Lead Qualifier to Calendar Booker).
A Multi-Agent System where a 'Planner' coordinates two 'Workers'.
